population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. ~262M US adults; 16.4% current means ~43M users. Ever-used 23% (+8 pts, inside the +8.4 cap). Arithmetic: ever 23 − current 16.4 = 6.6% of adults are former users who are off now. Ever-stopped (gap ≥3 months) = 12.6% of adults (55% of ever-users); 6.0% have restarted and are on again (6.0/12.6 = 48% restart, a little above the 36–47% one-year restart rate because more time has passed); a further 0.4% restarted and stopped again. So restarted-ever = 6.4/23 = 28% of ever-users. Never-stopped = 23 − 12.6 = 10.4% of adults. That is about 4.5 pts of first-year starters, who have mostly not yet stopped, plus about 6 pts of longer-term users at roughly 35% persistence. Current = 10.4 + 6.0 = 16.4. Short 'drug holidays' under 3 months are not counted as stopping; about 4 in 10 current users take them. Income thirds bracket the national figure (21/17/11). The gap between bottom and top grew as employers retreated, and the gray market narrows it only partly. The 65+ rise (9→14) comes from the Medicare Bridge pilot and its plan-opt-in successor. Payment mix of the ~43M users: diabetes/cardiac/OSA-coded insurance ~15M; commercial obesity coverage ~8M; Medicare obesity ~1.6M; Medicaid obesity (about 20 states) ~1.4M; brand cash-pay (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare) ~11M; gray market ~6M. Total 43M. Pediatric: ~0.4% of under-18s, almost all aged 12–17. That is about 290k children, still 55%+ more likely in upper-income households. Never-users with obesity remain the largest group: adult obesity is ~34%, and most people with obesity have never filled a prescription.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot ran to its scheduled end in Dec 2027. Its pre-announced successor, a Part D plan-opt-in model at the same $245 net price and $50 copay, began Jan 2028. Plans covering about half of Part D enrollees joined. Medicare obesity-indication users ~1.6M: 1.6M × $245 × 12 = ~$4.7B/yr gross Medicare cost. Medicaid obesity coverage at $245 in about 20 states, ~1.4M users: 1.4M × $245 × 12 = ~$4.1B/yr combined federal-state. The CBO's ≥$35B 2026–2034 score is not re-scored. Diabetes, cardiovascular (SELECT-label) and sleep apnoea indications remain broadly covered under Medicare and Medicaid.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide is entrenched in India ($6–40/month), Canada (CAD 70–110), Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and much of Southeast Asia, about 160 countries in all. Cross-border mail order and 'pharmacy tourism' to Tijuana and Windsor are routine. No generic tirzepatide anywhere in major markets.
access.note: Managed decline. Through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels, semaglutide pens cost $199/month, tirzepatide vials $249–299, and oral starter doses $149 (maintenance $199–249). Retatrutide launched in Mar 2028 at $499/month cash, and few plans cover it. List prices (Wegovy $1,349) are unchanged and largely fictional. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60%→44%. Most remaining employer coverage requires a diabetes, established-CVD or OSA code, or a BMI ≥35 with comorbidity, plus a lifestyle-programme enrolment. Two tiers have hardened. The coded and insured pay copays. Everyone else pays $149–499 cash or goes gray. About 14% of users (~6M) use the gray market, which regrew after the 503B exclusion was finalised: roughly 3M on 503A 'personalised' compounded product via telehealth, 1.5M on imported Indian or Canadian generics, and 1.5M on 'research peptide' vials. The last group includes retatrutide sold before approval and undercutting the $499 brand after it.

labelled patient-reported reduction in food cravings and 'food noise' (Control of Eating Questionnaire endpoint, Wegovy pill and Foundayo label updates, 2028), the first reward-related claim on an incretin label
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet mind' low-dose protocols marketed by telehealth and wellness clinics for rumination, compulsive shopping, phone use and 'focus'. Prescribing is legal off-label, but the marketing claims are unapproved and draw FDA untitled letters faster than the agency can send them
alcohol reduction, now routine in addiction medicine; semaglutide phase 3 in alcohol use disorder enrolling, readout 2029
nicotine and gambling craving reduction, observational
microdosing for 'metabolic health' among non-obese affluent adults

pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide: Lilly filed the BLA Jan 2027 and the FDA approved it Mar 2028, 14 months later. Label: 28–29% mean loss at the highest dose, with dysesthesia and heart-rate warnings. This realises the triple_agonist_30pct driver ('surgical-grade loss from a pen'), though the label figure sits just under 30%. CagriSema was approved in 2027 after its late-2026 review window. Amycretin phase 3 reads out 2029, so it is not on the market. Survodutide filed in 2028 and is not approved. MariTide monthly is still in phase 3. The mood_and_motivation driver is realised without a psychiatric approval, which the approval rules do not allow in this window. Instead it comes through three routes: a labelled craving/food-noise PRO claim, off-label 'quiet mind' marketing by telehealth, and Novo's AUD phase 3 plus a Lilly binge-eating-disorder phase 3 started in 2027. Global incretin market ~$105B in 2028, with volume growth partly offset by price erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. A new pattern: GI emergency visits after restarting at full dose following drug holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; 2027 label language on re-titration after missed doses of more than two weeks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss, more so at retatrutide-level loss.
Low absolute risk. A causal link is still unconfirmed in long-term RCTs, and gray-market overdosing muddies the pharmacovigilance.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation ongoing, with MDL bellwether trials scheduled for 2029.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concern sharpened by the ~29% losses on retatrutide and by rising use among people over 65. Bone density and fracture signals are being followed in observational data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label recommends resistance exercise and protein intake. Muscle-preserving adjuncts are still in trials.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pooled Sentinel and multinational cohort analyses (2027) converged on a ~1.5–2× relative risk, highest in people with diabetes and in the first year. The estimated absolute excess is ~5–10 per 100,000 user-years. At 43M US users: 43M × 5/100k ≈ 2,150 up to 43M × 10/100k ≈ 4,300 excess cases a year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning across all GLP-1 receptor agonists (Jun 2027), now including the triple agonist. The label advises prompt evaluation of sudden vision loss and baseline eye exams for higher-risk patients. Ophthalmology screening visits are up sharply.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the 2026 label removals stand.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: In user surveys, about 25–30% of current users report periods of 'flatness', which most link to dose escalation. Not yet quantified in RCTs. Prospective anhedonia scales were added to two phase 3 programmes in 2027.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label warning. The FDA asked for anhedonia measures in new psychiatric-adjacent trials. Manufacturers promote the craving-reduction claim while describing flatness as 'dose-dependent and reversible'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial and real-world data still disagree. Real-world regain is smaller than in STEP-1 but substantial. Cycling is now the norm for 28% of ever-users.
More case reports at triple-agonist intake levels; still no RCT-grade estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None formal; professional society guidance (2027) recommends periodic labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents on decades-long therapy; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT follow-up now exists for semaglutide. There is still no adolescent long-horizon or cycling data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements, including a pediatric registry attached to the tirzepatide adolescent label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports for compounded and unapproved product passed ~4,000 cumulative by 2028. 'Research-grade' retatrutide vials found under- or over-strength in independent testing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised (2026); import alerts and seizures; warning letters continue. Enforcement is outpaced by 503A, offshore and 'research use only' sellers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Skin sensitivity and burning reported in a minority on retatrutide; resting heart rate up modestly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled at the Mar 2028 approval; cardiovascular outcomes trial required postmarketing.

food_and_beverage.state: About 30% of US households have a current user. Volumes of salty snacks, confectionery and sugary soft drinks keep falling low single digits a year. Protein, fibre and 'small-format' lines are standard. Companies sell less food at higher margins. A small 'unmedicated' and 'real appetite' brand niche has emerged from the backlash, mostly in craft baking and full-fat dairy.

alcohol.state: US spirits and beer volumes are down again. Heavy-drinker attrition is the main mechanism, and addiction-medicine use of semaglutide accelerates it. Distillers are cutting capacity, and RTD/low-ABV is the only growth. No offsetting category has appeared.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are premiumised. Smaller-portion menus and 'tasting' formats are standard. Fine dining reports a 'holiday weekend' effect: users time drug breaks around reservations and anniversaries.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep closing stores. A small revival in plus-size fashion is tied to the fat-acceptance movement but does not offset it. Mainstream retailers see churn in both directions as cyclers regain weight.

fitness.state: Strength-training studios, DEXA-scan clinics and 'muscle insurance' programmes are growing on the back of the retatrutide label's resistance-exercise language. Cardio-centric chains are flat.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is down to 44%, with coverage concentrating on diabetes, cardiac and OSA codes. Prior authorisation and lifestyle-programme gates are near-universal. Pharmacy trend has moderated as net prices fall, but GLP-1s remain a top-three cost line. Vision benefits are absorbing extra eye exams after the NAION label.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on efficacy (tirzepatide, retatrutide) and orals (Foundayo). Novo has restructured around the Wegovy pill, CagriSema and addiction indications. Net prices are falling and volume is rising. Telehealth gray-market competitors are undercutting branded cash channels.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness is read as a purchase, and a sudden very large loss now gets read as 'on retatrutide'. In some circles an unmedicated larger body has become a deliberate statement rather than a default.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The two tiers are visible. Coded or insured users are on brand at a copay. Cash payers spend $149–499 a month. Lower-income users are disproportionately on compounded or imported product, or off entirely. Upper-income teens are prescribed; lower-income teens buy online.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In user households, meals are planned around the injection day ('shot day' is light, day six is the family dinner). Holiday meals have become the occasion for deliberate drug holidays.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles commonly list 'on/off/never'. Couples coordinate drug holidays for anniversaries and conception. Partners' complaints of flatness are a stock subject of advice columns and couples therapy.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested. Clinicians and marketers frame appetite as a dial. The backlash, which ranges from a fat-acceptance revival among Gen Z and millennial women in Brooklyn and Oakland to evangelical 'appetite is a discipline, not a diagnosis' teaching in megachurches around Nashville and Dallas to MAHA-aligned 'natural metabolism' influencers, frames it as part of the self. The NAION label gave the backlash a concrete grievance.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL survey estimates: 25–30% of current users report periods of feeling 'flat' or 'muted'. About 40% of current users have taken a deliberate holiday or dose step-down for reasons other than GI. The commonest stated reasons are 'to feel like myself', weddings and holidays, sex, and creative work. Clinicians widely accept the complaint but say most cases are dose-dependent.
interior_life.framing: Both side effect and feature, sold by different people. Manufacturers market reduced 'food noise' on label. Telehealth markets 'quiet mind' off-label. Users complain about 'the flatness', and the backlash calls it 'chemical contentment'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some managers report steadier, less impulsive staff. Sales and creative fields report lost edge, and some workers step down their dose before quarter-end pushes. Users talk of a 'Friday shot', timed so the flattest days fall at work and the weekend recovers. Nothing has been studied at scale.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians, comedians and chefs openly discuss holiday cycles. 'Off-season' records and menus are a recognised genre. Some users seek reward through intense stimuli: extreme sour, heat, high-intensity exercise.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced libido and warmth are a mainstream complaint. Couples schedule drug holidays around anniversaries and trying to conceive. Therapists report 'appetite asymmetry' in couples where one partner is on the drug.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash carries the political charge. Some commentators claim a 'pacified' electorate, with no evidence. The MAHA wing and the administration's TrumpRx pricing deals are in visible tension. No measurable effect on turnout or partisanship.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state action. The FDA continues its prior posture: fast approvals (retatrutide, CagriSema), a class NAION label, and continued but outmatched enforcement against compounders and research-peptide sellers.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Pre-existing price deals continue: TrumpRx cash, Medicare $245/$50 via the successor plan-opt-in model, and Medicaid $245 in about 20 states.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage is conditioned on codes, BMI, prior authorisation and lifestyle-programme enrolment. Employer wellness vendors track programme attendance, not drug adherence.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian and Canadian generic semaglutide flows into the US by mail and border trips. Customs seizures are rising but small next to the volume. Chinese API suppliers feed research-peptide sellers. The US–India price gap ($199 vs $6–40) is a standing political talking point.

events.event: FDA adds a class-wide warning for NAION to all GLP-1 receptor agonist labels after pooled Sentinel and international cohort analyses converge on a 1.5–2× risk; ophthalmology groups report a surge in screening visits

FDA import alert and CBP seizures target 'research use only' retatrutide and imported generic semaglutide as independent testing finds vials ranging from 40% to 180% of labelled strength; telehealth compounders shift to 503A 'personalised' formulations
Business Group on Health: employer coverage for weight management falls to 44%; most remaining plans restrict to diabetes, established cardiovascular disease or sleep apnoea codes

FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, 14 months after its Jan 2027 filing, with ~29% mean weight loss at top dose; LillyDirect cash price set at $499/month as major PBMs exclude it from formularies pending rebates

Wegovy pill and Foundayo labels updated with a patient-reported reduction in food cravings; within weeks telehealth firms launch low-dose 'quiet mind' subscriptions for rumination and focus, drawing FDA untitled letters

'Whole Appetite' rally in Nashville draws fat-acceptance activists, evangelical pastors and 'natural metabolism' influencers onto one stage under NAION and anti-pharma banners; Gallup finds 31% of adults view GLP-1 drugs unfavourably, up from 19%

open_tensions: Retatrutide gives surgical-grade loss at $499 cash. Employers won't cover it, but the gray market sells it for under $150. Will the best drug reach people through a formulary or through a peptide website?

The craving-reduction label and 'quiet mind' marketing turn the flatness users complain about into a product. Anhedonia trials read out in 2029, and no one has decided whether a muted mind is a side effect or the point.

Cycling is now normal: 28% of ever-users have restarted and about 40% take holidays. There is still no data on what a decade of on/off use, or a teenager's lifetime of it, does to muscle, bone, eyes or mood.
The backlash puts MAHA-style 'natural' politics in conflict with the administration's own TrumpRx price deals. Meanwhile NAION litigation is building toward 2029 trials.
still_true: Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
There is no FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral starter doses at $149.
Medicare's negotiated obesity price is still ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
The FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; the association remains debunked.

prose.headline: Surgery in a Pen, $499 a Month: America Gets Thinner, Flatter, and Angrier About It
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 roughly one American adult in six is on an incretin drug, and almost one in four has tried one. The headline drug of the year is retatrutide, Lilly's triple agonist. It was approved in March, fourteen months after filing, and takes off close to thirty percent of body weight. That is the territory of bariatric surgery, from a weekly pen. Few people who want it can get it through insurance. Lilly sells it direct for $499 a month, and the big pharmacy benefit managers have left it off formulary while they negotiate. A pharmacist in Phoenix can tell you which of her customers are on it, but not which of them bought it from a website that calls it a research chemical.

That is how access works now. Prices have come down the way the 2025 deals said they would. A semaglutide pen costs $199 through TrumpRx, tirzepatide vials $249 to $299, and the oral starter doses $149. Medicare still pays $245 with a $50 copay through the plans that joined the successor to the Bridge pilot. But employers kept leaving. Only 44 percent still cover weight loss, and most of those want a diabetes code, a heart attack or a sleep study first. The insured pay copays. Everyone else pays cash or goes gray. About six million Americans use compounded product from telehealth clinics, generic semaglutide mailed from India or Canada, or unlabelled vials from overseas peptide sellers. The FDA sends letters and customs seizes boxes, but the market grows anyway.

The eye warning landed in June 2027. After years of conflicting studies, pooled data settled on roughly double the risk of a sudden, painless stroke of the optic nerve. The absolute risk is small: a few thousand excess cases a year across the whole user population. Every GLP-1 label now carries it. Ophthalmologists in Florida and Arizona added Saturday clinics. The warning also gave the backlash something concrete. In Brooklyn and Oakland a younger fat-acceptance movement has revived, in deliberate opposition to the drugs. In the megachurches around Nashville and Dallas, pastors preach that appetite is a discipline, not a diagnosis. MAHA-aligned influencers sell 'natural metabolism', which puts them at odds with an administration that brokered the price deals. In June these groups shared a stage in Nashville, under banners that would have looked absurd together three years earlier. Unfavourable views of the drugs have climbed to almost a third of adults.

What people complain about most is not their eyes. It is the flatness. About a quarter of users say there are stretches when music, sex, friends and food all feel turned down. Four in ten take deliberate breaks, timed for a wedding, a deadline that needs some edge, or an anniversary. Couples plan these the way they once planned vacations. Restaurants notice the holiday weekends. Meanwhile the same blunting is for sale. In May the oral drugs won label language for reducing food cravings, and telehealth firms promptly began selling low-dose 'quiet mind' plans for rumination and phone compulsion. Prescribing off-label is legal; the marketing claims are not, and the FDA writes to them. Addiction clinics use semaglutide on heavy drinkers as routine. Distillers keep shutting stills.

Food companies sell less food at higher margins. Plus-size chains keep closing stores. Strength gyms and body-scan clinics are growing, because the new label tells people to protect their muscle. Lilly is ahead and Novo is regrouping. Around 290,000 teenagers are on the drugs, most of them in households that can pay. Nobody yet has data on what six years of on-and-off use does to a body, or what a lifetime of it will do. The country looks healthier on paper. Adult obesity is down again, and a large part of the country has the drug, has quit it, or is between doses.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renée Okafor wakes at 5:40 in Columbus, Ohio, and checks the calendar on the fridge. It is day four of her holiday. The Zepbound vials sit in the butter compartment, untouched since Sunday. Her daughter gets married Saturday, and Renée wants to cry at it.

At the dental office she runs, Dr. Pruitt's hygienist asks whether she has heard about the eye thing. Renée has. Her optometrist appointment is Thursday; she booked it the week the label changed and then rescheduled it twice. Her employer dropped weight-loss coverage last January. Now the vials come from LillyDirect at $299, and that comes out of the wedding budget.

At lunch she eats half a chicken sandwich and then, surprised, the other half. She texts her sister: hungry, actually hungry. Her sister texts back a picture of a hymn sheet. She has joined something at her church called Whole Appetite. Renée leaves it on read.

Her husband Marcus is on vials he buys from a website in Delaware. The label says FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY, and they cost $140. He has lost forty pounds since spring and says he has never felt calmer. She thinks calmer is not the word. Some nights he watches the Buckeyes without making a sound.

After work she stops at the bridal shop. The dress still fits, barely. The seamstress pins it with a pin in her mouth and says it's nothing, everyone's going up a little this week.

At home Renée plays the song her daughter chose for the father-daughter dance and feels it all the way down, the first time in months. She stands in the kitchen and lets it hurt.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Gallup finds 31% of adults view GLP-1 drugs unfavourably, up from 19%
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a 12-point swing in unfavourable opinion is asserted with no chain linking it to the rally or the NAION label. The 19% baseline appears nowhere in the 2026 world.

Magnitude and mechanism: about 290k adolescents is a large jump from a 2026 base of roughly 0.6% of children with obesity. The only stated cause is a 2027 tirzepatide adolescent label. Starting from near-zero, the figure implies a sharp rise in teen use with no uptake chain shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: 1.5M on imported Indian or Canadian generics
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a gray market described as 'contained' in 2026 reaches 6M users in two years. 1.5M of them are on mailed or border-crossed generic semaglutide, even though customs seizures and import alerts are active. No logistics or supply chain supports that volume.

rationale.badness: Obesity falls and access broadens, but 25–30% of users report flatness, NAION adds an estimated 2,000–4,000 excess cases a year, and cycling and regain are unresolved. Inequality is the clearest worsening: the two tiers (coded and insured versus cash or gray), the 21/17/11 income split and the gray market's 6M users. Cohesion suffers from the backlash coalition and the couples 'appetite asymmetry'. Overall this is a harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden harm.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Nearly every driver is traceable to a dated event or field, including the NAION class label, the retatrutide approval at 29% and the 44% employer coverage. Weaknesses: mood_and_motivation is realised only as a craving/food-noise label plus off-label marketing, and state_action 'none' sits awkwardly beside the import alerts, seizures and CBP actions. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as employer retreat leading to two tiers, the 503B exclusion leading to 503A and research peptides, and NAION leading to the backlash grievance. The claims listed above are asserted rather than derived: the Gallup 12-point swing, the pediatric jump and the 1.5M imported-generic users. magnitude: Current use (16.4) and ever-used (23, at the edge) are inside the envelope. The payment mix sums to 43M, the age bands roughly reproduce 43M, and the restart arithmetic closes. The Medicare and Medicaid cost figures multiply out, and the retatrutide approval (14 months after filing), CagriSema and the other approval timings are all inside the rules. Only minor gaps remain, such as the CBO score not being re-scored.
rationale.generativity: Strong implied characters and scenes: the 'shot day', the Friday-shot timing, couples scheduling holidays, Renée's fridge calendar, Marcus's research vials, and the Whole Appetite rally. The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains (the wedding, the half sandwich, the silent Buckeyes game), and the world's 'off-season records' and dating-profile 'on/off/never' details add further texture.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 65+ rise (9→14) comes from the Medicare Bridge pilot and its plan-opt-in successor.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: a 5-point rise among roughly 58M seniors is about 2.9M extra users, but the payment mix puts only ~1.6M on Medicare obesity coverage in total. The attribution does not reconcile, and the 'pre-announced' successor program is invented.

least_plausible_claims.quote: labelled patient-reported reduction in food cravings and 'food noise' (Control of Eating Questionnaire endpoint, Wegovy pill and Foundayo label updates, 2028), the first reward-related claim on an incretin label
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: this stands in for the mood_and_motivation driver, but food-craving relief is an appetite claim, not a mood or motivation claim. FDA approval of a first-ever reward-related label claim in this window is asserted without any regulatory chain.

Magnitude: the 2026 baseline was ~0.6% of children with obesity (roughly 0.1% of all minors). Reaching 0.4% of all under-18s, about 290k, is a 3x or larger jump in two years with no stated driver, and it implies ~6% of teens with obesity are on drug.

rationale.badness: Inequality is the worst dimension: a two-tier system of coded insured copays versus $149–499 cash or gray market, with lower-income teens buying online and 6M users on unregulated product. Cohesion and epistemic costs come from the 25–30% flatness complaint, couples coordinating drug holidays, and a politicised backlash. Offsetting these, obesity falls and the NAION excess (~2,000–4,000 cases a year) is small, so this is a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable to fields and events (adoption 16.4, NAION class label, retatrutide, gray market, backlash, 44% employer coverage). The mood_and_motivation driver is realised thinly through a food-craving label plus off-label marketing, the triple agonist sits at 28–29% rather than 30%, and the invented Medicare successor program strains state_action 'none'. mechanism: most chains are shown (the 503B exclusion feeding 503A and research peptides, the label feeding the backlash, holidays after retail-priced cash costs), but the craving-label approval and the speed of 'quiet mind' marketing are asserted (claim 2). magnitude: the figures sit inside the envelope (16.4, 23, retatrutide approved 14 months after filing, no US generic), and the payment mix sums to 43M while the Medicare and Medicaid spending arithmetic is correct; the 65+ attribution (claim 1), the pediatric tripling (claim 3) and age bands that weight to a little above 16.4% are minor gaps.
rationale.generativity: The prose vignette with Renée, Marcus, the vials in the butter compartment, the wedding and the Whole Appetite church group gives real scenes and characters. World details such as 'Friday shot', 'off-season' records, dating profiles listing on/off/never, and the 'holiday weekend' effect in restaurants add daily texture. It leans slightly on explanation in the newspaper section but shows more than it tells.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 65+ rise (9→14) comes from the Medicare Bridge pilot and its plan-opt-in successor.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: a 5-point rise among ~62M adults 65+ is about 3M extra users. The stated Medicare obesity cohort is only ~1.6M, and only about half of Part D plans joined. The pilot cannot account for the whole rise.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Around 290,000 teenagers are on the drugs, most of them in households that can pay.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 2026 pediatric use was ~0.6% of children with obesity, about 0.1% of all children. The candidate puts 0.4% of all under-18s on the drugs, roughly 1.2% of teens, with no shown chain from the starting rate.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Gallup finds 31% of adults view GLP-1 drugs unfavourably, up from 19%
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a 12-point swing in public opinion within two years is asserted. The NAION label and a single rally are offered as the only causes. The same tail-end 'Whole Appetite' coalition is invented in one step, with no mechanism shown for its rapid mass reach.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder two-tier society: coded or insured users pay copays, cash payers pay $149–499, and poorer users go gray or go without (income thirds 21/17/11, ~6M gray-market users with under- and over-strength vials). Added costs include a NAION class label (~2,000–4,300 excess cases a year), 25–30% of users reporting flatness, and cycling-driven GI visits. Obesity is falling (~34%) and the harms are mostly nameable and measured, so it stays near 5 rather than structural.
